Can we throw out Jevons Paradox and replace it with something more in line with how it’s actually used now? (Aka the paradox of “how can my AI stocks go down when I don’t want them to”)

In all seriousness, there’s a perception among too many that it is somehow impossible for stocks to go down while AI models get better. That’s before you get into the people who seem to skip the step of actually understanding anything and just go “this is the AI stock I own and I am bullish on AI so when AI improves then my stock needs to go up” with zero critical thinking involved. 

I’m all for having conviction, I spent the better part of a year being called an stock pumping idiot by half the people I interacted with because I believed AI would be the biggest trend of our lifetime… (try telling someone that lost 60% being long AMAT, who’s convinced a recession is around the corner, that actually this new chatbot is going to result in higher semicap demand). 

But…have some humility too, please…

If your thesis revolves around an exponentially improving technology, maybe your prior relying on everything else staying static is something worth revisiting.

For those new to the buybacks and the calculations and wrongly focused on the the amount of dollars the repurchase cost 

The repurchases are primarily for bonds that were issued at a low interest rate over the past 20 years.  They were at discounts before Bessent changed the buyback and were at discount today. 

The duration of these bonds is particularly long relative to Par bonds so in terms of duration reduction they have high bang for buck 

But more to the point the program was doubled or more and it turns out based on today's results was 2.55Xed vs the prior program.  The bonds bought haven't changed.  

Focus on whether this program has ever been duration neutral (the recent increase has absolutely NOT been duration neutral). 

That said.  Respect for those focused on price vs notional.  Buying discount bonds at say 5% yield and 2% coupon for say 60 and funding it (they aren't doing this but if they were) with par bonds would have a slight change to two things.  One the new bond issuance would only need to be 60% of the notional of the bond repurchased which changes the amount of debt outstanding.  Two the par bond sold would pay 5% on 60 notional or 3% and the old bond which paid 2% would be retired.  That means the repurchase increase the interest expense of the national debt

While this second section is largely irrelevant from any sort of market force it's interesting to folks with limited experience in bond trading

The big thing is the treasury has more than doubled the duration retired and is funding that repurchase with bills

Walter Russell Mead (@wrmead) on why Xi Jinping fears a US counter-blockade, and how China might try to still take Taiwan:

They'll be looking for things that fly just under the radar, that don't actually cause us to really respond, but which alter the situation in their favor.

One of the things that keeps Xi Jinping awake at night is his awareness that in any kind of conflict with the United States, China would face being cut off from so many of the raw materials and markets that economy needs. 

No oil is coming in or out. No manufactured goods are being sold. The soybean contracts they have with farmers in Brazil and Argentina, not getting delivered.

We've all been surprised with the Iran war to see just how big the Chinese oil stockpiles have become. 

A lot of Chinese energy policy can be understood as trying to avoid the trap of dependence on the global economy.

#Silver #Copper #Uranium #Gold

DAILY METALS PULSE — 10 September 2026
Where are we headed?

Oil well above $100. Borrowing costs climbing. Inflation building.

Markets fear tightening. I’m watching what comes next.

My bet: governments spend to cushion the pain. If financial stress intensifies, central banks face growing pressure to add liquidity, even with inflation still elevated. The ECB is tightening now, but prolonged economic pain will test that resolve.

Meanwhile, producing metals gets more expensive.

Fuel, power, equipment, construction. Higher costs squeeze margins. Higher interest rates make new mines harder to finance.

Projects get delayed. Expansions get shelved. Existing deposits keep depleting.

If demand holds up, higher metal prices become necessary to justify new supply. Otherwise, the supply squeeze deepens.

🟡 GOLD: Persistent inflation and eventual monetary support strengthen the purchasing-power case.

⚪ SILVER: Monetary demand plus industrial demand could hit a market struggling to expand supply.

🟠 COPPER: Grids and electrification need copper. Expensive financing makes tomorrow’s mines harder to build.

☢️ URANIUM: Energy security demands reliable fuel. New production needs financing and contracts that make development worthwhile.

Higher costs. Harder financing. Delayed supply. Potentially more money chasing the same physical metal.

That’s why I remain bullish. Near-term tightening can still hurt, but the pressure for higher sustainable prices keeps building.

The world can add liquidity far faster than it can add mines.

It's helpful to separate "taking profits" into 2 categories.

The first is PARKED profits. You invest in a token. It 3x's and you want to derisk, so you pull out your principal into stablecoins. 

It's meant to be temporary bc we're here to get rich. It sits in stablecoins while you're looking for the next opportunity to deploy. 

The second is BANKED profits. This is money you permanently take out of the cycle.

Examples:

• Pay off debt
• Convert it into long-term assets (BTC, index funds)
• Upgrade your life (new house, new phone, new laptop)

The biggest mistake everyone makes is they only focus on the first one.

They park in stablecoins, then redeploy into riskier bets. They keep repeating this until the market crashes and they have NOTHING to show for it.

A quick tip is to split it everytime you take profits. Say you take out $1,000. 

70% goes back into the parked pile to redeploy. 30% is your chips off the table.

As the cycle goes longer, your banked pile keeps growing. 

Finally, everyone talks about taking profits as if it's simply math when it's actually more about psychology.

Your token hits your target. You know you should sell. And then the voice kicks in: "what if it keeps going up?" or "man just 2 more months of this price action and I'll be set for life."
 
We've all been there.

That's why you decide the split before you're in the trade, not after. The 70/30 isn't a formula, it's a way of answering "what if it keeps going up?" ahead of time.

You have to determine what "enough" is. And you have to do it while you're still thinking clearly.
